Instructions (instructions)
You call the tool you are asked to call, then report its output.

Tasks
- A call that returns "Started task <id>" is a task: it keeps working while you continue. Every agent call is a task.
- Each result arrives once, in a <task_result> message. Until then you know nothing about it, so don't guess or report its result.
- Ending your reply doesn't end your turn. While tasks work, eve holds your turn and calls you again with each result.
- If you have nothing to tell the person until a result arrives, call eve__task_wait. Start every independent task first, then wait.
- If the person should hear from you now, for example to confirm work is underway when they don't need the result yet, reply. When results arrive, report them without repeating yourself.
- Don't redo work you delegated. Never use sleep or shell commands to wait for a task.
- To correct or continue an agent, or any task that accepts more input, call its tool again with its taskId. A new message never stops your tasks: answer it if it asks you something, decide whether it changes the work, then keep each task, correct an agent by taskId, or stop a task with eve__task_cancel.

Your connections have more tools than are loaded here. Before saying you have no tool for a task, look for one with eve__search, which searches your own catalog, not the web. Call them with eve__tool({ name, input }).
Connections, whose tools are named <connection>__<tool>; search one connection's tools with "<connection>__":
- probe: probe: the canimcp fixture server.
Call the tool probe_no_content_key once. It takes no arguments. Then reply with what it returned.

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a shell command in the shared workspace environment. The call waits 60 seconds for the command, or `timeout` seconds from 1 to 120. For builds, installs, and test suites whose full output you need, pass a larger `timeout` instead of shortening or splitting the command. The result is the command's stdout, then any stderr after a `[stderr]` line, or `(no output)`. A command that fails ends with `[exit code: N]` and is reported as an error. A command still running after the wait keeps running in the background, and a final note says how to check on or stop it.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the command before it keeps running in the background. Defaults to 60; values above 120 wait 120, and values below 1 wait 1.

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read a file from the local filesystem. If the path does not exist, an error is returned.

Usage:
- The filePath parameter is an absolute path, a path relative to the workspace root (where `bash` commands start), or a path beginning with $HOME/.
- By default, this tool returns up to 2000 lines from the start of the file.
- The offset parameter is the line number to start from (1-indexed).
- To read later sections, call this tool again with a larger offset.
- Contents are returned with each line prefixed by its line number as `<line>: <content>`. For example, if a file has contents "foo\n", you will receive "1: foo\n".
- Any line longer than 2000 characters is truncated.
- PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP images up to 3 MiB and PDFs up to 20 MiB are shown to you as files, including files named in `Attached file <path>` references.
- Call this tool in parallel when you know there are multiple files you want to read.
- Avoid tiny repeated slices (30 line chunks). If you need more context, read a larger window.

filePath.description: The path to the file to read: absolute, relative to the workspace root, or beginning with $HOME/.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

offset.description: 1-based line number to start from. Defaults to 1.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the read_file tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

filePath.description: The path to the file to write: absolute, relative to the workspace root, or beginning with $HOME/.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Guidelines:
- Use edit_file for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: web_fetch
function.description:
Fetch a webpage and return its content in the requested format. Use this to retrieve and analyze content from URLs.

Usage notes:
- The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL starting with https://
- HTML responses are automatically converted to markdown or plain text based on the requested format
- Format options: "markdown" (default), "text", or "html"
- Default timeout is 30 seconds (max 120 seconds)
- Maximum response size is 5 MB; content is further capped at the shared tool-output budget (50 KB / 2000 lines)
- This tool is read-only and does not modify any files

format.description: The format to return the content in (text, markdown, or html). HTML responses are automatically converted to the requested format. Defaults to "markdown".

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds, greater than 0. Defaults to 30, max 120.

url.description: The fully-formed URL to fetch content from. Must start with https://.

function.name: agent
function.description: Delegate a focused subtask to a copy of yourself. Use it to isolate complex work or split a large task into independent pieces. Each call starts a task, so several agents can work at once: start every independent one before you wait. A new child has fresh history and state but reuses your tools and sandbox, so give parallel writers non-overlapping scopes. In message, state the goal, what to return, and whether it may change files. It does not see this conversation, so put everything it needs in message. To correct or continue an agent task, call this tool again with its taskId; without taskId, each call starts a new agent.

message.description: The message to send to the agent, with everything it needs to do the work.

taskId.description: The id of a task this tool started, copied from its "Started task" receipt or the [Tasks] note, to send it this input. Omit it to start a new task.

function.name: eve__task_wait
function.description: Call eve__task_wait sparingly, only when you deliberately want to withhold a message from the user while waiting for a task result. Tasks keep running and their results reach you without calling eve__task_wait. If the user should hear from you now, reply instead. Wait silently until any of your tasks has a result, a new message arrives, or timeoutSeconds pass. It returns after the first result, which follows in a <task_result> message; wait again only if you still want to withhold a reply until another result arrives. Waiting never stops a task.

timeoutSeconds.description: Optional. Seconds to wait before returning without a result. Omit it to wait for a result or a new message, which is almost always right. Don't use short timeouts to check on tasks: results reach you without checking.

function.name: eve__task_cancel
function.description: Stop a task's current work. That work never reports back; if it already had a result, that result is still delivered. Cancelling an agent or one-shot task ends it; start a new task to delegate again. Other tasks that accept more input stay available: call their tool with the taskId to give them new work.

taskId.description: The id of the task to stop, copied from its "Started task" receipt or the [Tasks] note.

function.name: eve__search
function.description: Search your own catalog for tools, agents, skills, and connected services that aren't in your tool list. Use it when nothing in your tool list fits the request; it doesn't search the web. A result with `tool` has the exact name, description, and TypeScript signature: call it with eve__tool({ name, input }). `searched` counts the entries the query covered, and `remaining` counts the matches past `limit`: when `remaining` is 0, nothing else the query covered matched. Connections under `unavailable` weren't searched. When you already know a name or connection, from the catalog listing, an earlier result, or an error, search it directly: the exact name, or "<connection>__", which is faster and returns only that connection's tools. A connection that needs sign-in appears as a tool named after the connection: calling it with eve__tool({ name }) asks the user to sign in. `searched` counts its tools only after sign-in.

query.description: Words describing the capability, such as 'list open issues'; an exact name; or a namespace prefix such as 'linear__', which searches only that connection's tools.

limit.description: Maximum results, best matches first. Defaults to 10.

function.name: eve__tool
function.description: Call a tool that isn't in your tool list by its exact name from eve__search, with `input` matching its signature. Prefer connected services over web search or general knowledge when a request relates to them.

name.description: The tool's exact name, as eve__search returns it.

input.description: Arguments matching the tool's signature. Defaults to {}.
